blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: More Burnaby real estate
Condo buildings in Central Park
Central Park House — 5987 Wilson Avenue

A 41-storey residential high-rise by Bosa Properties, built in 2025 per current listings, designed by Gensler Architects, steps to Patterson SkyTrain Station and Central Park. Listings describe 24/7 concierge, an indoor pool and hot tub on the 17th floor, a 2,000 sq ft fitness centre, sauna and steam rooms, co-work space and social lounge, with 1 parking and 1 locker for the units checked. Published positions in listing fields include pets: a rental listing for the building calls it pet-friendly, and one sale listing records "Pets Allowed With Restrictions" — registered bylaws govern; published age restrictions: Not confirmed.
Paramount II — 5899 Wilson Avenue

A concrete high-rise by Bosa, built in 1996 per current listings, described as a 134-unit development in a building directory's listing record ("134 Unit Development, Concrete"), just minutes to Patterson and Metrotown stations and across from Central Park. The same directory record is titled "Pets Allowed" for this building. One listing notes the neighbouring Paramount (5833 Wilson) has an updated envelope "unlike 5899 Wilson" — a single listing's characterization, flagged here as a depreciation-report / envelope question to settle on the Form B, not as a verified building condition. Published rental/age restrictions: Not confirmed.
Paramount — 5833 Wilson Avenue

A concrete building by Bosa in the heart of Metrotown / Central Park BS per current listings, with exercise centre, steam room and bike room. Build-year conflict: listings record 1994, while a building directory and another listing record 1995 — noted, not resolved. Unit count and published rental/pet/age restrictions: Not confirmed from the sources checked.
Aldynne on the Park — 5883 Barker Avenue

A concrete tower by Polygon, built in 2017 per current listings, directly across from Central Park and minutes to Patterson SkyTrain Station, with a fitness centre and lounge. A building directory records its strata bylaws as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed. (One older building page gives a different build year (2014) and a different street address for this name; the 2017 / 5883 Barker Avenue position is the one current listings and the building directory agree on, and the older page is not relied on.)
Place Meridian — 5967 Wilson Avenue
That listing's fields record pets as "No." Unit count and published rental/age restrictions: Not confirmed.
Central Park Place — 5652 Patterson Avenue

A listing for a unit at this address introduces it as "Central Park Place," Central Park BS, a concrete-frame building with 2 parking stalls and 1 locker for the unit checked, recorded in that listing as built in 1981. A rental-platform building profile gives the same name and address as 408 units, 21 stories, built in 1992 — the year conflict (1981 vs 1992) and the unit count are both single-source and are treated as not confirmed beyond the name and address. Published restrictions: Not confirmed.
Central Park Place — 4160 Sardis Street

A separate building carrying the same name, on Sardis Street north of the park: a building directory records it as built in 1977, with an exercise centre, outdoor pool, recreation centre, sauna/steam room, swirlpool/hot tub and tennis courts, and records its strata bylaws as: pets not allowed, rentals not allowed — the "rentals not allowed" line is VOID: strata long-term rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 (Bill 44), and it is flagged again in. The pets-not-allowed line is a pet bylaw, which remains enforceable — confirm both on the Form B. Unit count: Not confirmed.
Grand Central Park Place — 6128 Patterson Avenue
A building directory records Grand Central Park Place at this address, built in 1992. Unit count and published rental/pet/age restrictions: Not confirmed from the sources checked.
Wimbledon Club — 6188 Patterson Avenue
Unit count and published rental/age restrictions: Not confirmed.
Streets, schools and getting around Central Park

items.t: The Central Park sub-area is the residential area around Central Park in south-west Burnaby, on the Vancouver border at Kingsway, directly west of Metrotown. The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS sub-area; the residential area surrounds the park, between Boundary Road (the Vancouver border) and Metrotown, along Kingsway and Imperial Street — exact MLS boundary streets: Not verified. Heritage Burnaby describes the park itself as lying between 49th Avenue to the south, Kingsway to the north, Boundary Road to the west and Patterson Avenue to the east.

Where the condo stock concentrates: east of the park, on the Wilson Avenue / Barker Avenue / Patterson Avenue grid between the park and Metrotown — a 1990s Bosa concrete cluster (Paramount, Paramount II, Place Meridian), a 1970s–1990s Patterson/Sardis cluster (Central Park Place at two addresses, Grand Central Park Place, Wimbledon Club), one 2017 tower (Aldynne on the Park), and the sub-area's newest tower, Central Park House (2025), at the Patterson Station end of Wilson Avenue. Detached houses hold the streets north and south of the park itself.

Main streets: Kingsway runs along the park's north side and Imperial Street along the south; Boundary Road forms the west edge at the City of Vancouver border and Patterson Avenue the east side of the park. Wilson Avenue, Barker Avenue and Sardis Street carry the tower stock.
Transit anchors: Patterson Station (Expo Line) is at the park's north-east corner and Metrotown Station (Expo Line) is east of the park — two SkyTrain stations frame the sub-area.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Park

items.t: One name, three buildings, two tenures of use. "Central Park Place" is a 1977 residential building at 4160 Sardis Street, a residential building at 5652 Patterson Avenue whose build year sources dispute (1981 vs 1992), and an 18-storey Bosa office tower at 4555 Kingsway built in 2000. Any search, document order or depreciation-report request made on the name alone can land on the wrong corporation.

The park's edges are heritage-recorded, and they fix the sub-area's shape. Heritage Burnaby records Central Park's ceremonial entrance gate on Kingsway (associated dates 1913) and the Jubilee Grove Arch at Kingsway and Patterson Avenue (1939), and describes the park as lying between 49th Avenue, Kingsway, Boundary Road and Patterson Avenue — the same four edges the condo grid sits outside of, east of Patterson.
The newest tower was planned at a different size than it was listed at.

A neighbouring building's listing is marketing against this stock. A Paramount (5833 Wilson) listing sells its own unit partly on the claim that its building has an "UPDATED ENVELOPE unlike 5899 Wilson" — inter-building envelope comparisons now appear in live listing copy in this cluster, which is a prompt to read both buildings' depreciation reports, not a verified fact about either.

The BC Parkway runs through the park under the SkyTrain line. Central Park carries the BC Parkway trail through it beneath the elevated Expo Line — the Patterson-to-Metrotown walk that tower listings call "steps to the park" is a lit, paved parkway route, and it is also why the park-side buildings' transit pitch is a walk, not a station address, for every building except the Patterson-corner stock.

French Immersion sits inside the catchment conversation here. Listings that present Inman as "the school" for a Wilson or Patterson address overstate it; the catchment elementary named in tower listings here is Chaffey-Burke.

items.t: "Central Park BS" is the GVR board sub-area name as used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby: the residential pocket around Central Park in south-west Burnaby, from Boundary Road (the Vancouver border) to Metrotown, between Kingsway/Imperial Street and the park. Central Park itself is bounded by 49th Avenue, Kingsway, Boundary Road and Patterson Avenue. Street-by-street boundaries for the MLS sub-area are not verified — no City or board source read publishes them.
Transit anchors: Patterson Station at the park's north-east corner and Metrotown Station, both Expo Line.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Park BS

items.t: Three residential buildings here share near-identical names — Central Park House (5987 Wilson, 2025), Central Park Place (5652 Patterson, and again at 4160 Sardis) and Grand Central Park Place (6128 Patterson) — plus a same-named office tower at 4555 Kingsway that is not housing at all. A Form B ordered against the wrong "Central Park" building is a real error risk in this sub-area; verify the civic address, not the name.

Listing copy for the sub-area describes Central Park as a 222-acre park — the park is the reason the Wilson/Patterson towers market "parkside" living, and its formal bounds (49th Ave / Kingsway / Boundary / Patterson) put the park itself in nobody's strata.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Central Park
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Lot character, only: typical Central Park lot sizes are not verified at sub-area level — no official source read states them. The only sourced lot figures are the R1 SSMUH thresholds: a minimum lot area of 281 m² and a minimum lot width of 10 m, with the 280 m² / 281 m² unit-count thresholds in. These are zoning thresholds, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

Servicing, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable, and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Parcel-level servicing for a specific lot: confirm with the City.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR split is documented for this sub-area, and no ALR percentage is stated. Parcel-level ALR status is checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Hazard position: no area-wide flood or hazard designation for the Central Park sub-area was found in the sources read; parcel-level hazard status is a property-specific check and is not verified for individual lots.

Plan frame for any future proposal: Metrotown is Burnaby's regional city centre and downtown under the Burnaby 2050 OCP, and the City lists higher-density housing, including towers, walk-ups and townhouses, in the town centres; the 2050 OCP takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict — so a Kingsway- or Imperial-fronting lot's assembly value must be checked against the 2050 OCP / Metrotown framework, not an older map.

items.t: Nearby areas: Metrotown to the east, South Slope and Garden Village to the south-east, the "Central" sub-area (Canada Way / Deer Lake) to the north-east — a different sub-area — and Vancouver across Boundary Road to the west.

Roads and transit: Kingsway runs along the park's north side and Imperial Street along the south; Boundary Road forms the west edge at the City of Vancouver border and Patterson Avenue the east side of the park. Patterson Station (Expo Line) is at the park's north-east corner and Metrotown Station (Expo Line) is east of the park — two SkyTrain stations frame the sub-area. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

Parks, recreation, library, health: Central Park itself is the sub-area's centre — the large City park on the Vancouver border at Kingsway, with the BC Parkway trail running through it under the SkyTrain line. Bonsor Recreation Complex, in the Metrotown area east of the park, serves this side of the city (facility detail beyond that: Not verified). The library branch serving this area is the Bob Prittie Metrotown Branch, 6100 Willingdon Ave, east of the park. The city's hospital is Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St (Fraser Health); the Metrotown Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 102-4555 Kingsway, east of the park.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Central Park

items.t: Strata block (for completeness — no Central Park bare-land strata is verified): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Central Park ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Park

items.t: The park is the sub-area, the downtown is next door: Central Park's planning frame is not a neighbourhood plan of its own — it is the Metrotown town centre, Burnaby's regional city centre and downtown, directly east of the park. A lot's long-term value question here is a Metrotown-edge question.

blocks.text: Sources

faq.a: Central Park House (5987 Wilson Avenue, Bosa, built 2025) is the newest, ahead of Aldynne on the Park (5883 Barker Avenue, Polygon, 2017). A 2025 building is inside its 2-5-10 warranty window; confirm the warranty position for the specific unit, because the 2-year and 5-year components expire before the 10-year structural component.
faq.q: Which buildings are the newest, and does warranty remain?

faq.a: Three, counting the office tower. Residential: 5652 Patterson Avenue (a listing records it built in 1981; a rental-platform profile says 1992 and 408 units — unresolved) and 4160 Sardis Street (built 1977 per the building directory, with pool, tennis courts and a pets-not-allowed bylaw on record). Commercial: the 18-storey office tower at 4555 Kingsway, built by Bosa in 2000. Always quote the street address with the name.
faq.q: Two buildings are both called Central Park Place — which is which?

faq.a: Half of it is void. The "rentals not allowed" line cannot be enforced: strata long-term rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022. The "pets not allowed" line is a pet bylaw, which remains enforceable in BC — so a buyer with a pet should treat 4160 Sardis as no-pets until the registered bylaws on the Form B say otherwise, while a buyer planning to rent the unit out can rely on the rental voidness.
faq.q: A directory says Central Park Place (4160 Sardis) allows no rentals and no pets — is that right?

faq.a: Published positions differ by building: Aldynne on the Park — pets allowed with restrictions (directory); Paramount II (5899 Wilson) — "Pets Allowed" (directory listing title); Central Park House — pet-friendly per a rental listing, "Pets Allowed With Restrictions" in one sale listing's fields; Wimbledon Club — "Cats OK" in a listing's fields; Place Meridian — "Pets: No" in a listing's fields. Listing fields are not bylaws — read the registered bylaws for the specific building before writing.
faq.q: Are pets allowed in the other towers?

faq.a: The one detailed published record is Place Meridian (5967 Wilson Avenue): complete repiping and boiler replacement (2023), elevator modernization (2024), swimming pool rehabilitation (2024) and updated common areas (2025), per a current listing. For Paramount II, a neighbouring building's listing claims Paramount (5833 Wilson) has an updated envelope "unlike 5899 Wilson" — unverified marketing copy from another building's sale, and exactly the kind of claim the Form B and depreciation report exist to settle.
faq.q: What capital work has already been done in the older buildings?

faq.a: No — Central Park is the park-side sub-area on the Vancouver border west of Metrotown; "Central" is the separate Canada Way / Deer Lake civic sub-area to the north-east, with different stock and different numbers. (SnapStats, September 2026)
faq.q: Is Central Park the same as "Central"?

faq.a: No verified one — no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata or presale lot offering was verified. The market is built houses on the park-side streets and strata product toward the stations.
faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot in Central Park?

faq.a: 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots, and 6 on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop; minimum lot width 10 m and minimum lot area 281 m² for SSMUH lots, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified. With Patterson and Metrotown stations framing the area, measure the 400 m test on the actual parcel.
faq.q: How many homes can an R1 lot hold here?
Where is the Central Park sub-area in Burnaby?
faq.a: Around Central Park in south-west Burnaby, between Boundary Road (the Vancouver border) and Metrotown, along Kingsway and Imperial Street; "Central Park" is the GVR MLS® sub-area name and this site files it as Burnaby South (central-park-bs) (SnapStats, September 2026)

faq.q: Which schools are in or near the sub-area?
faq.a: Maywood Community Elementary (K–7), 4567 Imperial St, Chaffey-Burke Elementary (K–7), 4404 Sardis St, and the École Inman Elementary French Immersion program, 3963 Brandon St, with Moscrop Secondary, 4433 Moscrop St, and Burnaby South Secondary, 5455 Rumble St, the nearest secondaries; catchments are address-based — check the SD41 locator, and note French Immersion is a choice program, not a catchment.
